title: Rooms and movement
summary: A world as a dict of dicts, and a command loop that walks it.

steps.title: The project
body: Over five stages you will build a small text adventure, the classic way to practise everything at once: dictionaries as data, a parser, state, and saving to JSON.
A dusty hall with a grand staircase.

The **world is data**, not code: a dict of rooms, each a dict with a name, a description, exits (direction to room id) and items. The engine reads it. Adding a room means adding data, not writing an `if`. In C# you might model this with classes; in Python a dict of dicts is the idiomatic first step, and you can promote it to dataclasses later.

steps.prompt: Using the world from the starter, what does this print?
code: "desc": "A dusty hall with a grand staircase.",
"desc": "Shelves of old books line the walls.",
"desc": "It smells of old bread. A trapdoor leads down.",
"desc": "Dark and damp. Something glints in the corner.",
steps.explain: Exits map a direction to a room **id**, which you look up in `ROOMS` again. `.get(key, default)` handles rooms with no `locked` key.

steps.prompt: Why keep the world in a `ROOMS` dict instead of writing `if room == "hall" and direction == "north": ...`?
options: Adding or changing rooms is editing data; the engine code stays the same
Dicts are faster than if statements
Python has no if statement for strings
steps.explain: Data-driven design: the engine is written once and works for any map. It also makes saving the game easy later, because the state is plain data.

steps.title: Walk the house
prompt: The starter defines `ROOMS`. Write the engine:
- On start, and after every successful move, describe the current room:
A dusty hall with a grand staircase.
- Read commands, one per line, case-insensitive:
- `go DIRECTION`: move if there is an exit, else print `You can't go that way.`
Ignore items and locks for now: they come in later stages. The game starts in the `hall`.
solution: "desc": "A dusty hall with a grand staircase.",
"desc": "Shelves of old books line the walls.",
"desc": "It smells of old bread. A trapdoor leads down.",
"desc": "Dark and damp. Something glints in the corner.",

expect: A dusty hall with a grand staircase.
